comments.content: Mutating `h.container.Logger` on the shared container is not safe for concurrent requests. `ServeHTTP` can be invoked concurrently for different requests, so one request's `defer` can restore the original logger while another request is still executing, causing trace IDs to be lost or mixed between requests. Consider passing the context logger explicitly to `h.function`/`logError` instead of swapping the container's logger.

`withTraceInfo` appends the trace map to the end of `args`. For `*f` methods, the trace map is appended after the format arguments, which is fine for `fmt.Sprintf`, but for non-format methods the trace map ends up as the last argument. More importantly, `extractTraceIDAndFilterArgs` in logger.go only extracts the trace ID if it appears as a `map[string]any` in args; if a user legitimately logs a `map[string]any` containing a `__trace_id__` key, it will be silently stripped. Consider using a dedicated unexported type instead of a magic map key to avoid collisions.

When `format != ""` and `filteredArgs` is empty (e.g. `Infof("hello")` with no args), `fmt.Sprintf(format, filteredArgs...)` is fine. However, when the trace map was the only arg and format is empty, `filteredArgs` becomes empty and `entry.Message` is left as nil, producing a log entry with no message. This is an edge case but worth handling.

`extractTraceIDAndFilterArgs` silently drops any user-supplied `map[string]any` that happens to contain a `__trace_id__` string key. This is a surprising side effect for callers who log arbitrary maps. Use a private sentinel type (e.g. `type traceIDArg struct{ id string }`) instead of a magic map key to make the intent explicit and avoid collisions.
